div.head: II As 6.1
div.ab: Gif he þonne ætsacan wille ⁊ on ðam þrimfealdum ordale fúl weorðe, þæt he beo CXX nihta on carcerne; ⁊ nimen þa magas hine siððan ut ⁊ gesyllan þam cynge CXX scll' ⁊ forgildon ðone wer his magum ⁊ gongon him on borh, ðæt he æfre swylces geswice.

Gif he hit ðonne ætsacan wille ⁊ on ðæm ðryfealdum ordale ful weorþe, þæt he beo CXX nihta on carcarne; ⁊ niman ða magas hine syþþan ut ⁊ gesyllan ðam cyng CXX scill. ⁊ forgylden ðone wer ðæs mannes magum ⁊ gangen hi on borh, þæt he æfre swylces geswice.

Gif he his þonne oðsacan wille ⁊ on ðæm þreofealdum ordale ful wyrðe, þæt he beo CXX nihta on carcerne; ⁊ niman þa magas hine syððan út ⁊ gesellan þæm cyning CXX scill' ⁊ forgylden þone were þæs mannes magum ⁊ gangan him on borh, þæt he æfre swilces geswice.

Si abnegare uelint et in triplici ordalio culpabiles inueniantur, sint CXX noctibus in carcere; et cognacio eorum educat eos, et emendetur regi CXX sol., et occisum hominem reddant parentibus suis et eant eis in plegium, quod semper abstineant in similibus (super hiis abstineant in ęternum).

Gif he þonne ætsacan wille ⁊ on ðam þrimfealdum ordale fúl weorðe, þæt he beo CXX nihta on carcerne; ⁊ nimen þa magas hine siððan ut ⁊ gesyllan þam cynge CXX scll' ⁊ forgildon ðone wer his magum ⁊ gongon him on borh, ðæt he æfre swylces geswice.

Wenn er aber sich (dessen So) unschuldig erweisen will, jedoch im dreifachen Ordal schuldig befunden wird: dass er [dann] 120 Tage im Kerker bleibe, und die Verwandten ihn nachher herausnehmen und dem König 120 Schill. zahlen und das Wergeld [des Umgebrachten] an die Verwandten (dieses Mannes So Ld) entrichten und für jenen [Missethäter] in Bürgschaft [dafür] treten, dass er [hinfort] stets von dergleichen [Thun] abstehe.

But if he wishes to prove himself innocent (of it, So), and yet is found guilty in the threefold ordeal: that he [then] stay 120 days in prison, and the kinsmen afterwards take him out and pay the king 120 shillings and pay the wergild [of the slain man] to the kinsmen (of this man, So Ld) and stand surety for that [offender] [to the effect] that he will [henceforth] always desist from such [doings].

If, however, he wishes to deny it, and is found guilty in the threefold ordeal, he shall remain in prison for 120 days; and afterwards the relatives may take him out and give 120 shillings to the king and pay the wergeld [of the dead man] to his relatives, and stand as surety for the offender that he shall cease from such practices for ever.

If, however, he wish to deny it, and is convicted at the three-fold ordeal, he is to be 120 days in prison; and the kinsmen are afterwards to take him out and to pay 120 shillings to the king, and to pay the wergild to his kinsmen, and to stand surety for him that he will desist from such for ever.

Lesart So his oð- ist archaischer; s. o. 4²
The reading in So, his oð-, is more archaic; see above 4²
Also wenn die Tat nicht handhaft oder notorisch
That is, if the deed is neither detected in the act nor notorious
Milder als beim Herrenverrat 4 bringt hier Ordalfälligkeit nicht so wie Handhaftigkeit höchste Strafe. Das Gefängnis (s. d. Gl 6 d. e) dauert aber dreimal solange wie beim jungen Diebe 1, 3

More leniently than in the case of treachery to a lord, 4, liability to the ordeal does not here bring the highest penalty in the way that being taken in the act does. Imprisonment (see that word in Gl 6 d. e), however, lasts three times as long as for the young thief, 1, 3

Da hier nicht (wie in 6) Todesstrafe die Straf- und Bussgelder absorbiert, treten diese in Kraft; Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 157. 186. — Statt ‘Wergeld (s. d. Gl Z. 17)’ versteht ‘den erschlagenen Mann’ Q, was möglich und den Sinn nicht berührt. Vielleicht daher übs. Q die möglicherweise auch ihm vorliegende Lesung þæs mannes in suis; diese eignet dann der ganzen zweiten Hss.-Klasse, ohne darum archetyp sein zu müssen

Since here (unlike in 6) the death penalty does not absorb the fines and compensations, these take effect; Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 157. 186. — Instead of ‘wergild (see that word in Gl l. 17)’ Q understands ‘the slain man’, which is possible and does not affect the sense. Perhaps that is why Q translates the reading þæs mannes, which he too may possibly have had before him, by suis; this reading then belongs to the whole second class of MSS, without necessarily being archetypal on that account
Vgl. Gl Bürgschaft 6 c. Beim Ausbleiben von Bürgschaft tritt wohl, wie VI 1, 4, Todesstrafe ein
Cf. Gl Bürgschaft 6 c. If surety is not forthcoming, the death penalty probably follows, as in VI 1, 4
